title: New Tesla Roadster Revealed, and It Flies

body_markdown:
Tesla first started hinting at a replacement for its very first model—the Lotus Elise-based[Roadster](https://www.hagerty.com/media/market-trends/hagerty-insider/2008-11-tesla-roadster-digital-heart-analog-body-tempting-price/) —in the early 2010s. In late 2017, the company unveiled a concept version. A much more ambitious car than the original, this Roadster came with typical over-the-top Elon Musk claims like 0-60 in 1.9 seconds, 250-mph top speed, and a 620-mile range. Tesla took $50,000 deposits for preorders, and $250K for a “Founders Series” model. Then there were delays, and more delays, the latest of which was just earlier this month, when weather pushed the much-anticipated final reveal from October 1 to October 15.


But the October 15 reveal did happen, and it was one for the books. Held at the 4000-acre SpaceX testing facility in McGregor, Texas, this wasn’t your typical pull-off-a-car-cover-and-clap unveiling. The new Tesla Roadster (autonomously) drove upside down, did a barrel roll in the air, and it was claimed to have hit 60 in under a second.


X.com/Tesla


After introductions by Franz von Holzhausen (Chief Designer), Lars Moravy (Vice President of Vehicle Engineering), and Musk, the Roadster—described as “a collaboration with the world’s best car company and the world’s best rocket company—came out, a coupe finished in white and looking rather different from the concept first unveiled nine long years ago. And the demonstration went straight into the stunts. “By the way, success is not guaranteed… It’ll probably work, but if it doesn’t work, we’re at a safe distance,” quipped Musk.


X.com/Tesla


X.com/Tesla


X.com/Tesla


X.com/Tesla


The car then rolled up a giant, C-shaped strip of road until it was upside down and sticking to the road, with an audible sucking sound. It rolled back down the road, then back up, took off, rolled right side up in mid-air, and hovered safely back to the stage. If there hadn’t been a crowd of people there, it would have been easy to dismiss the whole thing as AI. The Roadster also jumped and rolled over a row of Tesla’s other current productions, including Cybercab, Cybertruck, and Semi Truck.


The stunt was made possible by “a fan suction system on the bottom of the car that can pull up to two Gs in order to make the car go upside down, then we borrowed some technology from SpaceX to do the rest.” The trio elaborated further, describing “carbon overlay pressure vessels… there’s two of them in the car. They are a total of 600 liters. There’s about 250 kilos of air and we have 10 nozzles to do all that work, and it’s using an advanced ultra-high-pressure air tank, so the car can recharge its air tank. It’s not like you need special propellant or anything like that.”


X.com/Tesla


X.com/Tesla


The fan system also reportedly provides enough traction to corner at “greater than 2g.” The car can be set in a “high downforce mode” or a “low drag mode,” and the rear wing has variable pitch to adjust downforce automatically based on driving conditions.


There are also four “thrusters” in the rear that look a bit like exhaust tips, and they provide a claimed 80 kilonewtons of thrust. The next stunt was a timed zero-to-60 run with those thrusters thrusting, and the reported time was 0.81 seconds.


X.com/Tesla


X.com/Tesla


Other specs include a top speed of over 230 miles per hour, two seats, steer-by-wire, and brake-by-wire. Musk also noted that this will, in the longer term, be “the only manually driven car that Tesla makes.”


Whether the Roadster will “crush every track record that has ever existed,” as Musk claims, remains to be seen. Some other things remain to be seen as well. Musk is “not sure it’s necessarily legal in all jurisdictions,” and the Roadster will not actually enter production until 2028. Pricing details weren’t discussed, but previous reporting indicates the Roadster will be in the $200,000-plus range.


There’s also the fact that this whole event was, well, a show. Despite being Tesla’s last “manually driven” car, the Roadster that flew through the air and hit 60 in under a second did so without a human being inside. And it isn’t clear what features, technology, and capabilities the Roadster will have when it (finally) gets delivered to human beings in (hopefully) a couple of years. Credit where credit’s due, though, nobody has ever done a car reveal like this.
